To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bimetalic ceria-Co-Cuelectrode was able to operate directly on methane and ethanol with high performance, without carbon deposition, at 800 °C.
a ceria-Co/Cu anode can operate with hydrogen, ethanol and methane as fuels with good performance, stability and coking resistance.
ceria-based anodes with a bimetallic Co-Cu composition can be successfully utilised in SOFCs to produce power from methane or ethanol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the utilisation of methane and ethanol as primary fuels, in solid oxide fuel cells, without any reformer, by employing a ceria-Co-based anode, with a small amount of Cu added to the composition.
the development of a new SOFC anode material for direct utilisation as a fuel cell of carbonaceous fuels.
the development of a new ceria-Co-CCu anode material for solid oxide fuel cell applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ceria-Co-CU is an effective catalyst for the direct utilisation of primary fuels in solid oxide fuel cells.
ceria-Co-CU is the most promising anode for SOFCs that operate with methane or ethanol as the fuels.
the ceria-Co-CU cell is the best performing cell in terms of power density and coking resistance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Co-Cu-based ceria anode is an excellent choice for the direct utilisation of ethanol and methane as fuel in SOFCs.
the bimetallicity of the ceria-based anodes is a promising route towards achieving high power densities, coking resistance and stability for SOFCs operating on primary carbonaceous fuels.
the ceria-Co-CU anode is an effective candidate for direct utilisation and conversion of methane or ethanol in solid oxide fuel cell applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a ceria-Co-based anode with the addition of Cu can operate with methane and ethanol fuels and that it is resistant to coking.
the ceria-Co-CCu anode can be a promising alternative to conventional Ni-based anodes in SOFCs for utilising primary carbon fuels.
ceria-Co-Cux-based anode is a promising material for the direct utilisation of carbonaceous fuels in a SOFC.
